clue.text: It's never this cat getting run over, when looking both ways before beginning to walk

indicators.note: the cat and the run-and-over letters come ahead of the walking letter

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: the run-and-over pair faces backwards and then forwards, so the letters read the same in both directions

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run and O for over; written forwards and then backwards they make a four-letter run that reads the same either way

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word walk is taken

explanation.surface: A cat about to cross a road is warned to look both ways before setting off, or it will be flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' is not a traffic accident but cricket: R and O, set out so they read the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying goes that the day after today never comes; when it arrives it has become today, so it never is that day.

clue.text: Lout in black jumper turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters run from the bottom upwards, so the word order is reversed

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumping animal
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A yob dressed in a black sweater has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater (British for a pullover); it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a rude, uncouth man with no manners.

clue.text: Swell quarters, altogether sweet

indicators.note: the word asks for the posh person and the two compass letters to be joined together as one word

parts.note: a swell, like a toff, is a smartly dressed upper-class person
the compass points are quarters; E (east) is one, taken twice

explanation.surface: A smart gent's living quarters are, all things considered, lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh person; 'quarters' sounds like lodgings but gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter is a kind of sweet, the British word for a candy.

clue.text: Carefully choose journalist welcoming new measure of resolution

indicators.note: the journalist takes the other letters in, as a host welcomes guests inside

parts.note: a hack is a slangy word for a jobbing journalist
DPI, dots per inch, measures the resolution of printers and scanners

explanation.surface: A reporter takes on a new way of judging image sharpness and picks the best.
explanation.definitionFit: To select individually by hand, with care, is the idiom's literal and figurative sense of choosing carefully.

clue.text: Kiss-and-cuddle accounts are for the birds

parts.note: to spoon is old-fashioned slang for kissing and cuddling
bills are accounts of money owed

explanation.surface: Steamy accounts of romance are dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the birds' is an idiom for worthless, steering away from the literal birds that are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged wading birds with flat, spatula-shaped beaks; the plural matches the clue's plural noun.

clue.text: French government with a Liberal left in charge

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: France's government includes a Liberal politician on the left wing in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Gaul, the old name for France, so it means French in character.

clue.text: Rich relative given gold ring by Uncle Sam

parts.note: a son is a family relative
or is the heraldic word for gold
O looks like a ring
Uncle Sam personifies the United States, abbreviated US

explanation.surface: A wealthy family member receives a gold ring from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like wealthy, but it describes a voice or sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A full, deep, resonant voice is described as rich, the same quality as this adjective.

clue.text: May claim this, from time wearing black

indicators.note: the black covers the time letter, so the time letter goes inside it as if wearing it like a coat

parts.note: sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black

explanation.surface: A woman might claim something because the hour is dressed in black.
explanation.walkthrough: May is Theresa May, the British prime minister whose 2017 election slogan promised strong and stable leadership; it pairs with the 25 across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan Theresa May repeated claimed her government would be steady and secure, the adjective she used.

clue.text: Ask for it?

definitions.meaning: to request something earnestly or call on a court to reconsider

explanation.surface: Somebody is told they brought trouble on themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make an earnest request, and the noun is the charm or attraction that 'it' stands for in slang.

clue.text: See 24
Led astray by party leader taken in by ridiculous load of nonsense

indicators.note: the party's first letter is held within the jumbled letters
something ridiculous is absurd, so these letters are thrown into a silly new order
the leader of a word is its first letter
led astray means sent off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has been misled by a party leader who was fooled by an absurd pile of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' shuffles the letters of 'load of' into FLADOO around P; 'astray' shuffles the letters of 'Led' into DLE, placed by them.
explanation.definitionFit: An old American slang word for foolish talk, a synonym of drivel.

clue.text: Loud music on tablet, after soft drink

indicators.note: the tablet's letter comes after the soft letter

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
rap is a style of music
P, piano, is the musical marking for soft
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone plays loud music on a tablet device after a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' looks like one phrase, but 'soft' gives P and 'drink' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappe is an iced, often blended, drink such as a frozen coffee or a liqueur over crushed ice.

clue.text: Support for key person in soap playing instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

parts.note: a tool is an instrument for doing a job

explanation.surface: A person who is central to a soap opera plays an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges INSOAP into PIANOS; 'key person' is a pianist, who presses keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist sits on this adjustable seat, so it supports someone who plays the keys.

clue.text: Cool phone?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the first word of the answer turned back gives dial, which means to phone

explanation.surface: A trendy phone, or perhaps a call that is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool and relaxed in manner, easy-going, unflustered.

clue.text: Have complete faith in lawyers? Not initially, when upset about first of burglaries

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the burglaries letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the opening letter of the word lawyers is dropped
only the opening letter of the word burglaries is used

explanation.surface: Do lawyers trust absolutely when they are distressed about a first burglary?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' leaves AWYERS, 'upset' shuffles it to SWEARY, and 'about' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear by something is the idiom for trusting or relying on it completely.

clue.text: Being a dad briefly involved frivolous repartee

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of dad is dropped

explanation.surface: Being a father, for a short while, meant getting caught up in silly banter.
explanation.walkthrough: BEINGADA, 'Being a' plus DA from 'dad briefly', is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted, playful exchange of teasing remarks; a synonym of banter.

clue.text: One that's played with Pelé and Lukaku recalled a King Power outing

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so what is left is read backwards
outing means these letters are put out of the footballers' names

parts.note: the Brazilian football great's name, written without the accent
the surname of the Belgian striker Romelu Lukaku
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A footballer who played alongside two star strikers at Leicester's King Power Stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' leaves ELE and LUKU, and 'recalled' turns ELELUKU round. King Power is the stadium of Leicester City, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A small four-stringed guitar from Hawaii is a musical instrument, something that is played.

clue.text: Extremely wary, in case needing to cross lake

indicators.note: the lake sits across the middle of the in-case word

parts.note: lest is a formal word meaning in case
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone is very cautious in case they have to cross a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of leery, meaning suspicious or cautious, so most cautious.

clue.text: Caper around with the ultimate in ostentation?

definitions.text: Caper around with the ultimate in ostentation?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about, mixed up
the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: Someone frolics about, showing off as much as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CAPER plus N gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To move with high springy steps in a showy way is to caper about flamboyantly.

clue.text: Setter perhaps loves the German whose assistance is not always welcomed

definitions.text: whose assistance is not always welcomed

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so the clue gives an example
love is zero in tennis, written O; two of them
der is German for the

explanation.surface: The crossword setter adores a German whose help is unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-meaning busybody who interferes in others' affairs, offering help that often irritates; the relative clause stands for a noun.

clue.text: Whence fortified wine once produced? On river there only, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each word, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A question about where a strong wine was once made, answered with a riverside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the first letters overlap: 'once produced' belongs to both.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese city on the Douro gave its name to port, the fortified wine shipped from there.

clue.text: Lovely place to live no one wants?

indicators.note: no one means without the one, so that letter goes

parts.note: desires means wants, as a verb
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nice home that nobody wants to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one' reads as nobody, but splits as 'no' plus 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents' shorthand for a desirable residence, an attractive house to live in.

clue.text: Rising late, without handy place for early retirement?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from the bottom up, reversed
without in its older sense of outside, so the dead word goes outside the near word

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late author
by means near at hand, handy

explanation.surface: Getting up late, someone lacks a convenient spot to retire early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here; 'Rising' turns DEBYAD up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch for daytime naps, where one might retire to rest early, before night.

clue.text: Kids' mother follows nose, right away finding party

indicators.note: the kids' mother comes after the nose
right away means the right letter is taken away

parts.note: hooter is slang for a nose
kids are young goats and a nanny is a female goat

explanation.surface: A mother follows her nose straight away and finds a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately but removes R from HOOTER; 'Kids' are young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering with folk music and dancing, a lively party.

clue.text: Cat with bad intention gets the bird

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
poor means bad, of low quality
will means intention, as in against one's will

explanation.surface: A cat with bad intent catches a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American nightjar named for its call; it is a bird.

clue.text: See 24 across
May claim this? Patience possibly needed

definitions.meaning: Theresa May, British prime minister, claimed her leadership was steady and powerful
Patience ... was the pen name of a British writer of sentimental verse

explanation.surface: What might a woman named May claim? Patience may be required.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May's 2017 slogan was 'strong and stable', pairing with 8 down; Patience Strong was a popular British greetings-verse poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in Theresa May's slogan, and the surname of the poet whose first name was Patience.

clue.text: One that reads the Mirror in Lens?

parts.note: the eye is what reads text
a looking glass is a mirror

explanation.surface: Someone who reads the Mirror newspaper does so through a lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Mirror' looks like the British tabloid newspaper, but is a looking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or single lens for helping vision; the question mark marks the definition by example.
